مُفْرِقٌ A she-camel whose young one has become separated from her, (S, O, K, TA,) as some say, (TA,) by death: (S, O, K, TA:) pl. ↓ مَفَارِيقٌ . (TA. [Thus in my original, not مَفَارِقُ.]) ―
-b2- And A she-camel that tarries two years, or three, without conceiving. (TA.) ―
-b3- And A she-camel having a return of some of her milk. (TA.) ―
-b4- And Anyone recovering from his disease. (Lh, TA.) ―
-b5- And Deviating from the right way or course, or from that which is right. (TA.) ―
-b6- And مُفْرِقُ الجِسْمِ, (thus accord. to the K, there said to be like مُحْسِنٌ,) or الجِسْمِ ↓ مُفَرَّقُ , (thus in the O,) A man (O) having little flesh: or fat, or plump: (O, K:) two contr. meanings. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
